title: MAGA Personified: There Is Nothing Funny About Natalie Harp

Actual Article Body:
Daily Kos Community

This content is not subject to review by Daily Kos staff prior to
			publication.

Last Saturday, President Trump was at a nationally televised college football game between the Tennessee Volunteers and the Texas Longhorns. More than 100,000 people were there. But at one point he appeared to be more interested in his personal aide Natalie Harp and whatever she was showing him on her laptop.

Natalie Harp is the newest “weird” character in the MAGAverse — and the object of fascination and derision in the mainstream media, especially among the liberal commentariat.

Harp reportedly carries a bag full of Trump’s personal care items. Trump’s detractors have had great fun laughing at Natalie Harp’s letters of devotion, and the way she chases the president while he drives away in a golf cart. She was also reportedly with him on a secret flight out of Turkey while members of the cabinet and press pool served as human decoys to potentially be killed by an Iranian attack on Air Force One.

There has also been rampant speculation about the nature of their relationship. That is largely a private matter — except to the degree it could make him vulnerable to manipulation or otherwise imperil the country.

I have little interest in Natalie Harp the person, or in the political gossip and rumor-mongering surrounding Trump’s King’s Court.

But I do care about what Natalie Harp represents and the damage she and the other members of Trump’s King’s Court are doing to the American people and the country.

How does someone this close to Trump shape his thinking, his behavior, and what he does next? The deeper and more urgent story is not who Harp is but what she symbolizes and embodies.

Harp, his so-called “human printer,” matters because a central part of her job is showing Trump positive and fawning stories about himself in the media. She is like a fascist fairy keeping him cocooned in his own twisted world.

That type of forensic question has been largely avoided by the American media as an institution in the Age of Trump and the country’s collapse into fascism. The failure to consistently ask and answer that question, along with the sanewashing and other types of normalization, is a huge part of how the disaster that is the Age of Trump was born, why it has continued, and why it has gotten much worse so fast.

Trump truly believes that he is perfect, if not divine. He has shown little interest in changing his policies or behavior even as his polling numbers are collapsing to 20% in recent polls. Trump is — as one of his biographers told me — the main character and hero in his own story that he is writing in real time.

The late social psychologist Robert Jay Lifton had a term for the kind of reality that Trump inhabits. In a 2017 conversation with journalist Bill Moyers, Lifton described it as a “solipsistic reality”:

Solipsistic reality means that the only reality he’s capable of embracing has to do with his own self and the perception by and protection of his own self. And for a president to be so bound in this isolated solipsistic reality could not be more dangerous for the country and for the world. In that sense, he does what psychotics do. Psychotics engage in, or frequently engage in a view of reality based only on the self. He’s not psychotic, but I think ultimately this solipsistic reality will be the source of his removal from the presidency…

The American president has particular power. This makes Trump the most dangerous man in the world. He’s equally dangerous because of his finger on the nuclear trigger and because of his mind ensconced in solipsistic reality. The two are a dreadful combination.

Never forget that President Trump commands America’s nuclear arsenal and the power to destroy the world.

Consider what happened last week.
